iterations.narrative:
The metabolomics dataset reveals a strong enrichment of metabolites mapping to **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** — the top pathway by far, with an extraordinary fold-enrichment of 603.3 (FDR = 0.0, 7 matched compounds). This pathway coordinates the interlinked metabolism of one-carbon units, amino acids, and phospholipid precursors, and its perturbation is biologically coherent with the diverse chemical classes observed.

**Key driver compounds** include phosphoserine (C01005), sarcosine (C00213), choline (C00114), S-adenosylmethionine (SAM, C00019), and adenosine monophosphate (AMP, C00020), all of which were confirmed to be annotated under map00260. Phosphoserine sits at the metabolic nexus of serine biosynthesis and feeds into the trans-sulfuration axis, while sarcosine occupies a branch point in one-carbon folate metabolism. Choline converges on the same network through its oxidation to betaine and subsequent donation of methyl groups to homocysteine to form methionine — the direct precursor of SAM. The presence of lipoic acid (C16241) and L-cystathionine (C02291) further implicates the trans-sulfuration and methylation arms of this pathway. KEGG graph traversal confirms a direct 3-hop metabolic relationship between phosphoserine and sarcosine (C01005 → C00065 → C00037 → C00213), placing them in the same functional module.

**Biological significance**: One-carbon metabolism is the cell's master regulatory hub for methylation reactions, redox defense, and nucleotide synthesis. Dysregulation — reflected here by coordinated changes in SAM, choline, phosphoserine, and sarcosine — is linked to hepatic dysfunction, neurologic impairment, and cancer progression. Elevated choline and phosphoserine suggest enhanced phospholipid turnover and methyl-donor demand, while SAM depletion signals compromised methylation capacity. The involvement of biocytin (C05552) and lipoic acid further hints at mitochondrial energy stress, as both serve as essential cofactors for oxidative metabolism. Collectively, the data point toward a treatment-induced reconfiguration of one-carbon and amino-acid metabolism with downstream consequences for methylation, detoxification, and bioenergetics.
